parts.text: The IGCSE class is investigating resistor combinations in circuits. The first circuit used is shown in Fig. 3.1. Fig. 3.1 A student measures the potential difference V 1 across lamp 1 and the current I in the circuit.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R 1 of lamp 1 using the equation R 1 = V 1 I . R 1 = ........................................[1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student uses the voltmeter to measure the potential difference V 2 across lamp 2, and the potential difference V 3 across lamp 3.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Using Fig. 3.3, record the student’s reading of V 2. Fig. 3.3 V 2 = ............................................

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Calculate the total potential difference V T across the three lamps using the equation V T = V 1 + V 2 + V 3 . V T = ........................................[1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student rearranges the circuit so that the lamps are in parallel with each other and the ammeter is connected to measure the total current I T in the circuit. He connects the voltmeter to measure the potential difference V P across the lamps. In the space below, draw a circuit diagram of this new circuit using standard symbols. [2]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Another student suggests that R P should not be equal to R 1 3 because the lamp filaments are hotter when the lamps are connected in parallel than when the lamps are connected in series. State one piece of evidence, that you would see during the investigation, that shows that the lamp filaments are hotter in the parallel circuit. .......................................................................................................................................... ......................................................................................................................................[1]
